html:
The guerrilla war of the PAIGC against Portuguese rule, from January 1963 to 1974, the most successful of the African wars against Portugal.

Led by Amilcar Cabral, the PAIGC won much of the countryside, ran schools and clinics in liberated zones, and got arms from the Soviet bloc and bases in Guinea. Cabral was murdered in Conakry in January 1973. In September 1973 the PAIGC declared independence at Madina do Boe, and many countries recognised it. Officers worn out by the colonial wars overthrew the regime in Lisbon in the Carnation Revolution of April 1974, and Portugal recognised Guinea-Bissau in September 1974, with Luis Cabral as president.
sum: The guerrilla war of the PAIGC against Portuguese rule, from January 1963 to 1974, the most successful of the African wars against Portugal.
